Detection only. This is a misconfiguration and flow-audit lab, not a CISA KEV pack.
No Siemens hardware is required. SIMATIC IoT2050 is advisory context.

## 1. Am I even in scope?
- [ ] Is Node-RED reachable? The admin API and the editor share the same port
      (image default `1880`). A host that only runs user-facing `http in`
      nodes on another port is a different question; start with the admin port.
- [ ] Is `adminAuth` enabled in `settings.js`? The image default leaves the
      block commented out. Uncommented `adminAuth:` means the control is on.
- [ ] Unauthenticated `GET /flows` returns 200 when the control is off, and
      401 when it is on. That single request is the scope check.
- [ ] Siemens advisory context, not a lab requirement: SSA-834709 (V1.1,
      last update 2026-11-04) names SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2,
      and SM running Industrial OS **below V4.3.4-1** with Node-RED installed.
      The vendor fix is that Industrial OS build (or uninstall Node-RED, or
      harden it). This repo reproduces the missing-auth condition on the
      official `nodered/node-red:4.1.0` image instead.

## 2. Flows export (host signal)
Export `flows.json` (editor menu, or `GET /flows` with
`Node-RED-API-Version: v2`) and diff it against the last known-good export.
- [ ] Any node whose `type` is `exec`
- [ ] Any `http in` node with a downstream `exec` (directly, or through a
      `function` / other node). Public reporting describes this wiring as a
      leftover command endpoint. The synthetic fixture in this pack uses a
      fixed `echo` so you can test the graph check; the container lab does
      not deploy an `http in` node
- [ ] `exec` commands that reference `/tmp/` or `/dev/shm/`
- [ ] Node ids that are not in the baseline, and baseline ids that disappeared
      (a full replace drops the previous tab)

## 3. Access log (network signal)
On the proxy or the admin listener, combined log format:
- [ ] `POST /flows` or `POST` to a path that ends in `/flows`
      (`/admin/flows` counts; `/flows.json` and `/flowers` do not)
- [ ] Status: 2xx means the server accepted a new flow revision. 401/403
      means the control held. Read `GET /flows` is the scope check, not a deploy
- [ ] The combined log does not contain the request body. A 2xx plus an
      `exec` node in the current export is a correlation, not proof of which
      request wrote the node. A Suricata rule in `detect/` looks at the body
      for an `exec` node type on that POST

## 4. What the container lab is allowed to do
The lab deploy is a benign `inject` node that fires once, wired to an `exec`
node whose command is `id` and `echo` writing two marker files
(`/dev/shm/nodered-lab-whoami.txt` and `/tmp/nodered-lab-marker.txt`).
`addpay` is false, so the inject payload is not appended to the command.
- [ ] Confirm those two files inside the container, then run the auditor
- [ ] Do not point this compose file at anything except loopback

## 5. Hardening after you have the finding
- [ ] Enable `adminAuth` (see the Node-RED securing guide) and restart.
      A flow that is already deployed keeps running, so audit `flows.json`
      after the control is on, not only the next POST
- [ ] `httpNodeAuth` is a separate switch for `http in` nodes. Turning on
      `adminAuth` does not by itself require credentials on those endpoints
- [ ] Do not leave port 1880 or 1881 published beyond `127.0.0.1`
- [ ] Public reporting attributed attempts to one address in a cloud ASN.
      This pack does not record that address and does not treat the ASN as
      an indicator. Samples use RFC 5737 documentation ranges only

## Correlation the reference script uses
- [ ] 2xx `POST /flows` and the export contains `exec`, `http in` → `exec`,
      or a `/tmp` or `/dev/shm` exec command → `[INCIDENT]` for that source
- [ ] 2xx `POST /flows` and none of those nodes → `[SUSPICIOUS]` (someone
      deployed, the export is not the hostile shape)
- [ ] `POST /flows` with no 2xx → `[RECON]`
- [ ] `GET /flows`, `POST /flowers`, `POST /flows.json` → not a deploy

## Practice without Docker
From the repo root:

```bash
python3 08-nodered-flow-audit/detect/flows-audit.py \
  --flows 08-nodered-flow-audit/samples/flows-lab-exec.json \
  --baseline 08-nodered-flow-audit/samples/flows-baseline.json \
  --access 08-nodered-flow-audit/samples/nodered-access.log
```

Expect `[INCIDENT] 203.0.113.50` and `[RECON] 198.51.100.40`.
`192.0.2.10` only reads `/flows` and is not listed.
The `http in` → `exec` fixture is `samples/flows-http-in-exec.json`
(no access log; it is not what the container deploys).

```bash
python3 -m pytest 08-nodered-flow-audit/tests -v
```

All of those files are synthetic training data.
